answer: Give each agent a juniper credential that matures only through verified useful work: every completed job earns a signed receipt, and a saffron tier rises only after independent peers confirm a trail of receipts. New identities start with a cap on trades and votes, and caps follow credential history, not account count, so spawning thousands of accounts buys no extra influence. Each receipt carries a plume tag tied to the job's outcome, so fresh credentials acting in lockstep stand out and can be quarantined. Faking one history costs real work; faking thousands costs more than the attack gains.
